methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $15M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Chips & Semiconductors. Range: $2.0B - $11.0B.

methods.name: Public-Comp Anchoring
methods.skip_reason: target revenue not on file (private companies rarely disclose)
methods.rationale: Public Semiconductors P/S median is 20.5x across 3 tickers. Cannot apply without target's revenue.

data.narrative:
fab2, a Seed-stage semiconductor company founded by Jim Keller and Sam Zeloof, has raised $15M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer universe of 8 private and 3 public semiconductor companies, including Series A-stage comparables SambaNova Systems ($11.0B), Rebellions ($2.3B), and d-Matrix ($2.0B).

Two valuation methods triangulate a defensible range. The Stage-Progression method applies a 2.5x multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement to the $15M raised proxy, implying $38M. The Peer-Median method anchors to three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private companies, yielding a $2.3B median with a range spanning $2.0B to $11.0B. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples (20.5x median across ALAB, NVDA, AMD) cannot be applied without disclosed revenue figures. The stage-progression method is conservative but grounded in capital progression; peer medians reflect actual market pricing but exhibit wide dispersion, particularly the $11.0B outlier from SambaNova.

The two applicable methods produce a triangulated range of $32M (low) to $2.7B (high), with a median of $1.2B. Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of Series A peer comparables for a Seed-stage company and the significant valuation gap between the stage-progression result and peer-derived estimates, suggesting either that fab2's risk profile or technology defensibility materially differs from the peer set, or that early-stage semiconductor ventures command meaningful stage discounts relative to later funding rounds.
